title: Odisha moves over 1 lakh people to shelters as Cyclone Akvan nears Friday landfall near Gopalpur
dek: The storm was 410 km south of Gopalpur at 2.30 pm on Thursday, moving north at 13 kmph, the IMD says; it warns of a storm surge of up to 1 metre in Ganjam and Puri at landfall around noon on Friday.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Odisha had moved 1,05,304 people to 1,224 cyclone and flood shelters by Thursday as Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan closed in on the coast, Chief Secretary Anu Garg said, more than double the figure the administration gave in the morning, and evacuations were still going on. Landfall is expected around noon on Friday, 20 November, between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha, close to Gopalpur in Ganjam district.

In its 5.30 pm national bulletin on Thursday, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said that at 2.30 pm the storm lay over the west-central Bay of Bengal about 410 km south of Gopalpur and 470 km south of Puri, moving north at 13 kmph, with maximum sustained winds of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph. It warned of a storm surge of 0.5-1 metre above the astronomical tide in low-lying parts of Ganjam and Puri and four north coastal Andhra districts at landfall. It is the third cyclone to threaten the same stretch of coast in about four weeks, after Arnab in late October and Murasu at the start of November.

## What happened

The storm picked up speed overnight, from about 5 kmph on Wednesday night to 12-13 kmph on Thursday, and has been moving steadily north. The IMD's forecast table shows the winds easing to 80-90 kmph by 11.30 am on Friday, close to landfall, and the storm then weakening quickly inland: to a deep depression, with winds of 50-60 kmph, by Friday night, and to a well-marked low-pressure area over Jharkhand by Saturday. The IMD expects extremely heavy rain of 21 cm or more at isolated places in Odisha on Thursday and Friday and in north coastal Andhra Pradesh on Thursday, and has flagged a moderate risk of flash floods in seven north Odisha districts, among them Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara and Balasore.

The morning count of evacuees was 46,701; by midday Garg put it at about 72,000, and later at 1,05,304, reports said. Ganjam accounts for the largest share, with 45,364 people moved, followed by Gajapati with about 18,000. About 9,000 pregnant women close to their due dates have been moved to health centres, and 9,299 shelters have been identified and stocked with rations, drinking water and medicines, reports said. "Zero casualty is our goal," Garg told reporters. Tourists have been barred from Gopalpur, Puri, Satapada and Chilika. More than 11,000 people have been identified for relocation in Jagatsinghpur. Pregnant women, children and elderly people are being moved first, and people in hilly areas have been told to leave because of the risk of landslides, reports said.

Reports differ on how many districts are under the IMD's red warning for extremely heavy rain on Thursday and Friday: some say 11, while the Chief Minister referred to 13. Ganjam, Gajapati, Malkangiri, Koraput, Rayagada, Kalahandi, Kandhamal, Puri, Khurda and Nayagarh are among the districts named. Schools and anganwadi centres are closed from 19 to 21 November in Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara and Kandhamal, and the Odisha Staff Selection Board has postponed recruitment examinations.

Fourteen National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams, 60 teams of the Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force and 221 fire service units have been deployed, and 100 forest corporation teams are standing by to clear fallen trees, according to reports. The state has released advance assistance of Rs 1 crore each to the districts expected to be hit and has sent seven IAS officers to oversee relief in vulnerable districts. The Water Resources Department has assigned senior engineers to watch river levels from Friday to Sunday, reports said.

"The state government is fully prepared and has already begun taking measures to address the situation," Majhi told reporters after a review meeting at the Special Relief Commissioner's office on Wednesday. He said avoiding any loss of life was the government's first priority.

In Andhra Pradesh, the state's Real Time Governance Society asked the north coastal districts of Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Kakinada and the Godavari districts to stay on alert for the next 24-36 hours, reports said. Fishermen along the Srikakulam coast have pulled their boats ashore as the sea turned rough, and strong waves were reported in Ranasthalam mandal. Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Alluri Sitarama Raju and Kakinada are the districts most at risk of very heavy rain, according to reports.

## Further afield

Three long-distance trains through the region were rescheduled on Thursday: the Charlapalli-Shalimar East Coast Express, the Secunderabad-Howrah Falaknuma Express and the Bengaluru-Muzaffarpur Express, reports said. Passengers have been asked to check train status before travelling.

The storm's northward track also brings it closer to West Bengal. The IMD forecasts heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places in Gangetic West Bengal on Thursday and Friday, and its 5.30 pm bulletin flags a moderate flash-flood risk in East Midnapore, Howrah, the two 24 Parganas and Nadia over the next 24 hours. Fishermen have been told not to go into the north-west and west-central Bay until Saturday morning.

## Background

Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast at the end of October, and its remnants caused floods and landslides in southern Odisha: three members of one family were killed in a landslide in Kandhamal and about 60,000 people were moved to safety across nine districts. Murasu crossed the coast near Ongole on 3 November and damaged crops on more than 30,000 hectares in Andhra Pradesh, without loss of life, according to the state government. The IMD has moved Akvan's expected landfall several times this week: from the stretch between Nellore and Visakhapatnam, which it forecast on Tuesday, north to the Narsapur-Puri window on Wednesday.

Odisha has made mass evacuation the centre of its cyclone policy since the 1999 super cyclone, which killed nearly 10,000 people in the state. The forecast landfall area around Gopalpur is in Ganjam, the district that took the brunt of Cyclone Phailin in 2013 and was flooded again by Arnab's remnants last month, so the ground is already saturated in many places.

## What happens next

The IMD issues national bulletins every three hours. Landfall is expected around noon on Friday, after which the storm should weaken over Odisha. The heaviest rain in southern Odisha and north coastal Andhra Pradesh is forecast for Thursday night and Friday, and the storm's remnants are expected to bring rain to Jharkhand, south Bengal and northern Odisha on Friday night and Saturday. The Declaration will update this story after landfall.

## Key numbers

- 1,05,304: people moved to shelters in Odisha by Thursday, according to the Chief Secretary (46,701 in the morning)
- 1,224: cyclone and flood shelters in use
- 90-100 kmph, gusting to 110 kmph: forecast winds at landfall
- 410 km: the storm's distance south of Gopalpur at 2.30 pm on Thursday
- 3: cyclones to threaten the Andhra-Odisha coast since late October
